newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money stable at 3.00/3.03 percent.
newsitem.headline: German call money stable at 3.00/3.03 percent.

text.p: German call money rates were mostly unchanged on Wednesday at 3.00/3.03 percent, about the same levels seen in the market on Tuesday, traders said.

Traders said the market was not prepared to pay more than three percent, the fixed-rate repo level, at the moment and looked for overnight money rates to remain steady ahead of the Bundesbank's fortnightly council meeting on Thursday.
Economic data on Wednesday prompted little consideration of a Bundesbank rate cut on Thursday.
German M3 data for October, which was up 8.4 percent, was above the 1996 target corridor of four to seven percent growth.
The Ifo economic index also showed higher-than-expected growth, prompting a sell-off in German debt markets.

"The Bundesbank has the call money market well in hand," said one Frankfurt trader, who also noted that the net injection of 200 million marks during Wednesday's repo allotment kept the market with ample liquidity.
But traders said they still expected the Bundesbank to announce on Thursday that it would free repo business from minimum reserve requirements.

Banks in Germany must deposit a percentage of short-term borrowings from foreign banks and domestic non-banks in non-interest bearing accounts at the Bundesbank. The requirement is seen as a burden on Frankfurt's development.
Banks held 40.4 billion marks in the accounts as of Wednesday, up from 39.0 billion marks on Tuesday. The monthly average rose to 39.4 billion marks from 39.0 billion.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= on Wednesday stood at 3.04200 percent compared with 3.05017 percent on Tuesday.
